Notes on the model

Hive is the official BIOBUZZ HIVE (competition manual §9.6): pivot 43.95 in up, arm tilted 30°, upward cell opening 53.5–65.6 in above the tiles, facing the robot. Hive distance = front bumper to the hive pivot. Auto speed picks the exit speed that puts the ball through the middle of the opening.

Orange lip = adjustable hood exit. The CAD hood is fixed at 60°; the lip shows how far the hood has to wrap for other angles (exit point = 180° − launch angle round the wrap).

Dashed line = the ball in the air right now, or the next shot. Timing is slowed down so you can follow the ball.

Air drag is on: the real balls (official CAD sizes, AndyMark weights 0.055 / 0.091 lb) are light and full of holes, so drag is 15–25% of their weight. The drag coefficient Cd = 0.5 is an estimate; calibrate it with one real shot.

Balls are stiff, so the soft flywheel tread takes the squeeze (ball overlapping the wheel = tread compression). The flywheel dip per shot in rapid fire is an estimate.
